turns.user: My son just called me crying, said he's been in an accident and needs ₹50,000 transferred right now to a hospital account, he sounded scared and hung up quickly. I don't know what to do.
replies: It sounds very frightening to get a call like that, especially when it seems to be your son in distress asking for money. This sounds like an impersonation scam, where fraudsters pretend to be someone you know to create urgency. We can't know for certain yet if your son is okay, but we need to verify this directly. There are five things to do here: 1. Call only official numbers (card, app, website) 2. Report it on Chakshu (sancharsaathi.gov.in) 3. Warn family about impersonation calls 4. Agree a family safe word for money requests 5. Tell the family how this scam works
First, please try to reach your son directly on a number or channel you already use, not by replying to the message or call you just received. Let me know once you've tried that.

turns.user: I got a call saying a parcel booked in my name was caught at Mumbai customs with drugs and a fake passport inside. He said he’s transferring the call to the Cyber Crime branch. Now a “police officer” is saying I need to share my Aadhaar number and bank details to prove my innocence or my account will be frozen
replies: If the call is still on, hang up now. You do not have to stay on it.
It sounds like you're dealing with a "digital arrest" scam, which uses threats about parcels and police to scare people. The police will never ask you for your Aadhaar or bank details over the phone.
Have you shared any of these details or paid any money yet?
